title: 7 July 1969: Recording: Here Comes The Sun
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, Abbey Road
Producer: George Martin
Engineer: Phil McDonald

George Harrison’s second song for Abbey Road, ‘Here Comes The Sun’, was begun during this 2.30-11.45pm recording session.

Harrison, Paul McCartney, and Ringo Starr recorded 13 takes of the backing track, on what was also Starr’s 29th birthday.

This was also John Lennon’s first recording session since his car accident in Scotland. Although he did not perform on the recording, he was present in the control room.

Take 13 – announced as “take 12 and a half” for superstitious reasons – was judged to be the best attempt, and featured Harrison on a Gibson J-200 acoustic guitar and guide vocals, McCartney on Rickenbacker bass guitar, and Starr on drums. In the final hour of the session Harrison taped an additional guitar part using the same J-200.

Take nine from the same session was included on some formats of the 50th anniversary reissue of Abbey Road, and on 2025’s Anthology 4.

Work on ‘Here Comes The Sun’ continued on the following day.

Page last updated: 12 February 2026
